title: Google Summer of Code
eligibility: Students 18+ enrolled in a post-secondary academic program or recently graduated (within 12 months). Open internationally.
description: A global program where students spend the summer writing code for open source organizations. Students receive a stipend and work with experienced mentors. GSoC spans 12-22 weeks and covers a broad range of open source projects across all programming languages.

title: Microsoft Explore Internship
eligibility: First- or second-year undergraduate students pursuing a degree in computer science or a related field.
description: A 12-week summer program for early-in-career students to explore engineering roles at Microsoft. Interns rotate across software engineering, program management, and data science. Full compensation and housing provided in Redmond, WA.

title: Meta University Engineering Program
eligibility: First- or second-year undergraduate students pursuing a BS or MS in computer science or related technical field.
description: A paid 12-week internship designed for students from underrepresented backgrounds. Participants work on real engineering projects at Meta alongside mentors and a cohort of peers. Housing assistance provided.

title: NASA Internship Program
eligibility: US citizens currently enrolled full-time in an accredited US college or university, minimum 3.0 GPA, 16+ years old.
description: NASA offers hundreds of internship opportunities across its 10 field centers. Interns contribute to real NASA missions in engineering, science, business, and communications. Paid positions; some include housing allowances.

title: Goldman Sachs Summer Analyst Program
eligibility: Penultimate-year undergraduate students from any degree discipline. Strong analytical and communication skills required.
description: A 10-week paid summer internship across divisions including Engineering, Investment Banking, Markets, and Asset Management. Interns work on live projects, receive mentorship, and are considered for full-time offers. Offices across London, New York, and other global cities.

title: Rhodes Scholarship
eligibility: Citizens of eligible countries aged 19-25 at time of taking up scholarship. Outstanding academic record required.
description: The world's oldest international graduate scholarship, supporting postgraduate study at the University of Oxford. Covers all University and college fees, a living stipend, and economy airfare. Around 100 scholars selected globally each year.

title: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
eligibility: Citizens of any country outside the UK, applying for a full-time postgraduate degree at the University of Cambridge.
description: Funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, this scholarship covers the full cost of study at Cambridge plus a maintenance allowance. Around 80 scholars are selected annually based on academic excellence, leadership potential, and commitment to improving the lives of others.

title: Chevening Scholarship
eligibility: Citizens of Chevening-eligible countries with at least 2 years of work experience and a UK university offer for a one-year masters degree.
description: The UK government's flagship international awards programme supporting outstanding individuals to study a one-year masters at any UK university. Covers tuition fees, living expenses, flights, and other allowances. Around 1,500 scholarships awarded annually.

title: Schwarzman Scholars
eligibility: Young leaders aged 18-28 from any country, applying to a one-year masters in global affairs at Tsinghua University, Beijing.
description: Designed to prepare future leaders to understand China's growing role in global affairs. The fully funded program covers tuition, room, board, travel, and a personal stipend. Up to 200 scholars selected globally each year.

title: Fulbright US Student Program
eligibility: US citizens with a bachelors degree by the program start date. Graduate students and early-career professionals eligible.
description: Provides grants for US graduating seniors, graduate students, young professionals, and artists to study, research, or teach abroad for one year. Covers living expenses, travel, and health insurance in 140+ countries.

title: Wellcome Trust PhD Studentships
eligibility: Applicants applying to a PhD programme at a Wellcome-supported institution in the UK. Biomedical and health research focus.
description: Wellcome funds PhD students at leading UK universities through its research training programmes. Studentships cover tuition fees, a competitive stipend, and research expenses. Strong emphasis on biomedical, genomics, and global health research.

title: Soros Fellowships for New Americans
eligibility: Immigrants or children of immigrants who are US citizens or permanent residents, aged under 30, in or planning a graduate program in the US.
description: Supports the graduate education of immigrants and children of immigrants in the United States. Awards up to $90,000 across two years (tuition support + living stipend). Up to 30 Fellows selected annually.

title: Innovate UK Smart Grants
eligibility: UK-registered businesses of any size, including startups, working on disruptive R&D projects with commercial potential.
description: Quarterly open competition awarding grants for game-changing or disruptive R&D ideas with the potential to create new markets. Projects between 25,000 and 500,000 GBP. Non-dilutive funding that does not require equity.

title: European Research Council Starting Grant
eligibility: Researchers of any nationality holding a PhD with 2-7 years post-doctoral experience, based at or moving to an EU or associated country host institution.
description: ERC Starting Grants support early-career researchers in establishing their own research team and launching an independent, frontier research project. Grants up to 1.5M EUR for 5 years. Highly competitive and peer-reviewed.

title: Thiel Fellowship
eligibility: Under 23 years old, willing to leave or skip college to pursue a startup or research project.
description: A two-year program awarding $100,000 to 20-25 young people each year to skip or stop out of college and launch a company or research project. Fellows receive funding, mentorship, and access to the Thiel network of investors and entrepreneurs.

title: Y Combinator Startup School
eligibility: Early-stage founders at any stage, any country. No age requirement; particularly suitable for student founders.
description: A free, 8-week online program helping early-stage founders build and launch startups. Top-performing startups from Startup School are fast-tracked to apply for YC's main batch, which includes $500,000 in funding.

title: Jane Street FOCUS Fellowship
eligibility: First-year undergraduate women and non-binary students studying STEM subjects, particularly math, computer science, or statistics.
description: A 5-day immersive program at Jane Street offices for early-career women and non-binary students to explore quantitative trading and technology. Participants attend workshops, solve trading puzzles, and meet Jane Street staff. Travel and accommodation covered.

title: Google DeepMind Scholarship
eligibility: Students from underrepresented groups applying to or enrolled in a masters in machine learning, AI, or a related field at a partner UK university.
description: Google DeepMind partners with top UK universities to fund masters students from underrepresented backgrounds in AI and ML. Scholarships cover tuition fees and provide a living stipend. Recipients also gain access to mentorship and DeepMind events.

title: Bloomberg Women in Technology Scholarship
eligibility: Women-identifying undergraduate students studying computer science or engineering in the US, UK, or India.
description: Awarded to outstanding women pursuing technology degrees. The scholarship covers tuition support and includes a paid summer internship at Bloomberg. Recipients receive mentorship and access to Bloomberg's global engineering community.

title: Shopify Engineering Internship
eligibility: Students in computer science or software engineering undergraduate programs. Remote-friendly; international applications welcome.
description: A co-op style program where students complete full-time paid internships at Shopify working on production codebases and real merchant-facing products. Strong remote-first culture with teams across the globe.

title: Palantir Path Scholarship
eligibility: Undergraduate students studying computer science, software engineering, or related fields who identify as underrepresented in tech.
description: Provides $7,000 grants to undergraduate students from underrepresented backgrounds pursuing degrees in technology. Winners are also invited to a paid Palantir Forward internship. Open to applicants in the US, UK, and Canada.

title: EPSRC Doctoral Training Partnerships
organization: Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council
eligibility: UK domestic students applying for a PhD in engineering or physical sciences. International students eligible for fees-only support at some DTPs.
description: EPSRC funds PhD studentships through Doctoral Training Partnerships at UK universities. Fully funded stipend plus tuition fees for 3-4 years of doctoral research in engineering, computing, mathematics, and physical sciences.

title: Venture for America Fellowship
eligibility: Recent college graduates from any major. US citizens or those authorized to work in the US.
description: A 2-year fellowship placing recent college graduates at startups in emerging US cities. Fellows receive entrepreneurship training, a living wage, and mentorship. Designed to jumpstart careers in innovation and build the next generation of entrepreneurs.

title: CodePath Tech Fellowship
eligibility: Computer science students at any US college or university, particularly those from low-income, first-generation, or underrepresented backgrounds.
description: Free, intensive software engineering courses paired with career coaching and recruiter connections at top tech companies. Graduates are placed in internships and full-time roles at companies like Google, Meta, and LinkedIn.

title: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
eligibility: Students aged 13-18 from any country who can submit a short video explaining a challenging scientific concept.
description: An annual global competition inviting students to produce a short video (under 3 minutes) that illustrates a concept in mathematics, life sciences, or physics. The winner receives a $250,000 scholarship and their teacher and school receive additional awards.
